header.title: Product and harness, not raw benchmarks, protect frontier lab economics

s01_bottom_line.text: SemiAnalysis prefers closed Fable 5 for daily work despite Kimi K scoring higher on its composite, and GPT-5.2 scored better than Opus 4.5 without a better user experience, because the full agentic product (model + harness) matters more than benchmarks.
The article argues it is 'less bearish frontier models than you might initially think' because benchmarks are an imperfect proxy and productization defends closed-lab economics.
If product/harness quality, not raw benchmark parity, drives real usage and revenue, open-model benchmark catch-up may overstate the commoditization risk to closed frontier labs like Anthropic.

items.text: Since the general release of Claude Code in May 2025, Anthropic has added north of $65B in ARR. ⟨cited figures: approximate⟩
GPT-5.2 scored better than Opus 4.5 on the benchmark suite but did not deliver a better user experience, because the full agentic product (model + harness) is what matters.
Although Kimi K scores higher than Fable 5 on the composite, SemiAnalysis still prefers using Fable for day-to-day work, partly due to Anthropic's productization.
The authors argue they are less bearish on frontier models than the catch-up trend might initially suggest.
